title: Joint Employer Status under the Fair Labor Standards Act, Family and Medical Leave Act, and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act
pass_4_primary_concern: The proposal standardizes joint-employer analysis across several statutes, but the record is thinest where it asks the public to trust qualitative burden claims and fact-heavy line drawing.
pass_5_concise_why: The proposal is structurally coherent, but its confidence claims rely on incomplete empirical support and judgment-heavy boundaries.
pass_5_most_important_consequence: Commenters can still shape the final boundary rules and push the Department to justify its nationwide cross-program standard more fully.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal leans on a broad cross-program regulatory rewrite rather than a narrow, program-specific fix.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask why a narrower FLSA-only or program-specific approach would not solve the same problem.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The Department reads the FLSA definitions as supporting a new, more uniform joint-employment framework across related statutes.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for the strongest text-and-precedent basis for the cross-program move.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: A nationwide rule change can shift the practical leverage of contract and staffing arrangements before field guidance is fully settled.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask whether the final rule should phase in or better stage implementation guidance.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The Department acknowledges missing prevalence data and relies heavily on qualitative estimates for the main impact story.

evidence.quote_or_absence: does not currently have data on the number of businesses that are or might be in joint employment relationships
the analysis below ... is qualitative due to data limitations and inherent uncertainty

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for prevalence estimates or a reasoned explanation of why quantification is impossible.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal promises clarity and uniformity, but the remedy is broad enough that the notice does not fully show why this exact cross-program rewrite is the best fit.

evidence.quote_or_absence: clarity and a measure of uniformity
the Department considered three alternatives to the proposed rule

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask why a narrower rewrite, staged approach, or program-specific exception would not work as well.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule expects investigators, employers, and courts to apply a layered factor test consistently in real time.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for model examples and investigator guidance that show how the rule works outside the preamble.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule suggests recurring savings will exceed initial familiarization costs, but the public record still leaves much of that claim qualitative.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask the Department to show the main recurring savings it expects and how they compare with the upfront costs.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: Businesses may try to structure arrangements to avoid joint-employment treatment at the margins of the rule.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask how the Department will prevent strategic sequencing or contractual relabeling from undermining the rule.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal offers examples and factor language, but the boundary safeguards are still somewhat open-ended for close cases.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The Department welcomes comments on all aspects of proposed § 791.115(f)
whether consideration of the number of contractual relationships ... should be expressly excluded or included or not addressed

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for clearer exclusions, examples, or decision rules that make the carveout enforceable.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The cross-reference structure is clear, but it can make later tracing of program-specific reasoning harder than a separately reasoned rule would.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for a short crosswalk showing how each program-specific provision maps to Part 791.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule itself does not impose immediate duties, but it can still alter how parties sequence work before final review in the field.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask the Department to explain why pre-final uncertainty will not create avoidable costs or pressure.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal shifts more decisions into the pre-enforcement and pre-dispute phase, so the gateway needs to stay understandable and reviewable.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for concrete guidance on how the later compliance gate will stay independent and transparent.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal divides business practices into relevant and irrelevant categories, but the downstream consequences of that split are not fully mapped.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask the Department to map the consequences for common arrangements like franchise systems or staffing models.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule still allows judgment-heavy gating at the margins, which can invite inconsistent administration.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for more objective guardrails around the most common borderline scenarios.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal is coherent overall, but the breadth of the rewrite means the final text will need careful drafting to avoid drift across programs.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask the Department to provide a short crosswalk and examples showing how the parts fit together.
